subject: Discovery recap — Nomad Retail (embeddings / rerank)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Discovery recap — Nomad Retail (embeddings / rerank)

Hi Jane + Tom,

Great to meet today — thanks for taking the time to walk through Nomad's search & recommendations goals. Per our call, below is a short recap of pain, current stack, and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain / goals
- Search relevance has dropped after catalog growth (~3M SKUs). Click-through and conversions on product search are down ~12% YoY.
- Current relevance stack struggles with recall at scale; results are noisy for long-tail queries.
- Primary goal: improve relevance for both search and recommendations with embeddings + reranking, while keeping 95th percentile latency under 150ms for query paths.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Primary storefront search: Elasticsearch (self-managed) with custom scoring.
- Vector DB: Pinecone for nearest-neighbor embeddings (index sharded by tenant).
- Feature store: internal feature service, offline batch updates nightly.
- Traffic: ~1.8k qps peak across global regions (US-heavy), with most queries batched for nightly offline ranking.
- Average product catalog size: ~3,200,000 SKUs; working set per query ~5k–20k candidates depending on filters.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- +6–10% improvement in search CTR and add-to-cart for query-led sessions within 60d of POC.
- End-to-end 95th pct query latency <= 150ms on read path (embedding lookup + rerank).
- Vector index costs not to exceed current budget by >25% (goal: similar or lower).

Workload details we documented
- Index scale: ~3.2M vectors, 768-dim embeddings (plan to experiment with 512/384 quantized variants).
- Vector DB: Pinecone today; open to migrating to Redis or FAISS-backed managed solution for throughput/cost.
- Batch patterns: nightly full re-embed (offline) + incremental micro-batches during the day for new SKUs (~5–10k items/hr).
- Query patterns: 85% single-vector queries (top-k retrieval) followed by model-based rerank of top 200 candidates.

Immediate next steps
1) Redwood POC proposal and pricing (I attached a brief requirements doc).
2) Marissa will coordinate the contracts/PO path if we move forward.
3) Rishi (cc’d) to join a technical sync to validate latency targets and propose an initial POC architecture (end of week).
4) Proposed POC scope: 30-day effort — 50k query sample set, 1 shard of the live catalog (~500k vectors) for staging, compare Pinecone vs Redis-FAISS cost/latency.

Attachments: nomad_poc_requirements.pdf (POC checklist & data needs), redwood_pricing_v2.pdf (baseline estimate)

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical sync.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila — recap looks accurate. Couple clarifications/questions from our side: 

1) Vector dimensionality: our embeddings team currently produces 768-dim vectors from a fine-tuned model, but they're open to a 512-dim model if that materially reduces cost without hurting quality.
2) Budget: we have a rough monthly budget target for vector infra and reranking of ~$30k–$40k. Important this stays within reason for the long term.
3) Latency: 150ms 95th for the entire stack (nearest-neighbor + ML reranker) is aggressive but is our business target — will need to see real numbers from a POC.

We’re happy to host the first technical sync on Friday at 10am PT. Tom will pull in a data engineer and our embeddings lead.

Hi Jane / Camila / Marissa,

Thanks — looking forward to the sync Friday. A few technical notes / assumptions so we can jump into architecture quickly:

POC assumptions
- Staging shard: we’ll sample ~500k vectors (~768 dims initially). We’ll also test 512/384 quantized variants to measure recall vs size tradeoffs.
- Query load: use a 50k query sample (real production logs) replayed to staging at stepwise QPS (100 qps, 500 qps, 1k qps) to observe tail latency.
- Rerank: model will run on GPU (recommended) for top-200 candidate rerank to keep latency predictable; CPU-based microservices possible for lower-cost experiments.

Latency/cost expectations (early estimates)
- Pinecone (managed): expected NN p95 on 500k shard ~40–90ms depending on dims & replica config; add GPU rerank ~30–70ms p95 => combined ~90–160ms p95.
- Redis + FAISS (managed/self-hosted): NN p95 could be lower-cost at scale if we use PQ/IVF quantization (512/384 dims) but requires careful sharding and memory tuning; combined p95 potential ~80–150ms.
- Key levers: quantization (reduce index size), candidate K (top-200 vs top-50), and batching of rerank requests. If we can reduce rerank to top-50 for most queries, latency drops substantially.

Data-ingest & incremental updates
- We recommend an append-with-ttl approach for micro-batches and periodic compaction in the POC. For their 5–10k items/hr incremental rate, streaming ingestion into a write-optimized replica and async compaction should be sufficient.

What I’ll bring to the sync
- Concrete staging architecture diagram (Redis+FAISS and Pinecone variants).
- Cost model spreadsheet and assumptions.
- Baseline test plan for 50k query replay and measurement scripts.

If there are any specific latency SLAs or ops constraints (multi-region reads, failover windows), please paste them here and I’ll bake them into the plan.

— Rishi
